about: Every source the Atlas cites. 'supports' says which claim the source backs, so a reviewer can check it quickly.

sources.title: Universe overview
sources.supports: General chronology of the universe; starting reference for the project.

sources.title: The Cosmic Microwave Background (Astronomy 2e, 29.4)
sources.supports: The early universe was hot and opaque until atoms formed a few hundred thousand years after the Big Bang, when it became transparent.

sources.title: Slime Mold Simulations Used to Map Dark Matter Holding Universe Together
sources.supports: The cosmic web is mostly dark matter laced with gas; galaxies form along its filaments, which are mapped from galaxy surveys.

sources.title: Quasars: Cosmic beacons (News & Views, Nature 514, 2014)
sources.supports: Quasar numbers peaked about 10 billion years ago and have declined steadily since.

sources.title: A portrait of the black hole at the heart of the Milky Way
sources.supports: EHT imaged M87* (2019) and Sgr A* (2022): a bright ring around a dark shadow. Sgr A*'s event horizon would not reach Mercury's orbit; M87*'s would reach about as far as Voyager 1.

sources.title: Nobel Prize in Physics 2020, press release
sources.publisher: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
sources.supports: Genzel and Ghez tracked stars orbiting an invisible, extremely heavy object at the centre of our galaxy.

sources.title: How to take Hubble-like photos: Filters and post-processing guide
sources.supports: Hydrogen-alpha emission is deep red; doubly ionised oxygen (OIII) is blue-green.

sources.title: Webb snaps supersonic outflow of young star (HH 211)
sources.supports: A Class 0 protostar, an infant analogue of the Sun, fires a narrow bipolar jet.

sources.title: Lifetime of a Star
sources.supports: The Sun was born about 4.6 billion years ago from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust.

sources.title: Revolutionary ALMA Image Reveals Planetary Genesis (eso1436)
sources.supports: The disc around the young star HL Tauri shows concentric bright rings separated by gaps, likely carved by forming planets.

sources.title: The Birth of the Solar System (Astronomy 161)
sources.supports: Small rocky planets formed in the hot inner nebula; giant planets formed beyond the frost line, where ices survive.

sources.title: Earth's sun: Facts about the sun's age, size and history
sources.supports: The Sun has fuel for about another 5 billion years, then swells into a red giant, sheds its outer layers and leaves a white dwarf.

sources.title: Iridescent Glory of Nearby Helix Nebula
sources.supports: The Helix Nebula is about 650 light-years away; its ring is nearly 3 light-years across.

sources.title: Webb finds surprises in Spiderweb protocluster field (weic2428)
sources.supports: The Spiderweb protocluster is a galaxy cluster in formation, with more than a hundred known galaxies, seen as it was over 10 billion years ago.

sources.title: Two of the Milky Way's Spiral Arms Go Missing
sources.supports: Spitzer showed the Milky Way has two major arms (Scutum-Centaurus and Perseus) joined to the ends of a central bar, with two minor arms between them.

sources.title: Pillars in the Eagle Nebula from Hubble (2014)
sources.supports: The pillars are cold hydrogen gas laced with dust, with stars being born deep inside; denser regions shadow the material beneath them from the radiation of nearby stars.
